title: Aun así: reconocer un contraste a pesar de lo dicho

sections.content: Aun así (even so, nevertheless) acknowledges a fact just stated and then pivots to something surprising or contrary to what that fact might lead you to expect -- useful for data-driven writing that needs to hold two seemingly contradictory truths together. It typically opens a new clause or sentence. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Muchos países retomaron cierto crecimiento económico; aun así, este crecimiento no se tradujo en una reducción de la desigualdad.
items.english: Many countries regained some economic growth; even so, this growth didn't translate into reduced inequality.

items.spanish: El producto interno bruto regional crecía, aun así, sin generar suficientes empleos formales bien remunerados.
items.english: Regional GDP was growing, even so, without generating enough well-paid formal jobs.

items.spanish: Las cifras de pobreza extrema mejoraron; aun así, la riqueza se concentró todavía más en los sectores más ricos.
items.english: Extreme poverty figures improved; even so, wealth concentrated even further among the richest sectors.

items.spanish: Este contraste alimentaría, aun así, un creciente descontento popular durante la década siguiente.
items.english: This contrast would nevertheless fuel growing popular discontent over the following decade.

sections.content: Aun así works like sin embargo, but leans more directly on the previous sentence's content -- it says despite what I just told you, this is also true, whereas sin embargo can introduce a more independent contrast.
